name: Rigidity of the Six Fixed Two-Row Contractions of the 267-Concept Obstruction
statement: For each of the six two-row presentations of the labelled $267$-concept obstruction, fix the two large rows $D_0,D_1$ and put $C=D_0\cap D_1$. Among every pair $B_0,B_1\subseteq C$ with $B_0\cup B_1=C$, the four-row assembly $(B_0,D_0,D_1,B_1)$ is ample and cornerless only for the original diagonal-row assignment and its exchange. Thus each fixed contraction has exactly two labelled solutions, both of order $267$, and no smaller cornerless ample assembly.
proof: The fixed crossed family $(D_1,D_0)$ is ample, so the exact two-row identity reduces ampleness of the assembly to ampleness of $(B_0,B_1)$. A Boolean encoding expresses shattered-equals-strongly-shattered for this two-layer family and directly excludes a corner at every possible retained vertex. Complete model enumeration yields precisely the original rows and their exchange for each of the six contractions. Adding clauses that block those two assignments produces six independently checked DRAT refutations. Direct reconstruction verifies all twelve surviving models, and separate at-most-$266$ refutations agree with the minimum order.
comments: This is a finite rigidity theorem for six labelled contractions. It does not classify cornered negative assemblies, assemblies with changed large rows, or establish a global $267$ lower bound.
